text:
diego: Hey team - I got married in Peru on Oct 20 but the civil registry is taking forever to issue the US-recognized certificate. I missed the 30-day QLE window for adding spouse to benefits. Anyone know if exceptions are possible?
maya_peopleops: Congrats! Typically QLE is 30 days but there are limited exceptions for delayed foreign documentation. Can you DM the wedding docs you have (ceremony attestation, wedding photos, passport stamps)? We'll start an exception request.
diego: I can upload a marriage affidavit from the local municipality and passport entry stamps. I don't have the official translated certificate yet; embassy says 6-8 weeks.
sam_peopleops: Upload what you have to Workday -> Benefits -> Upload eligibility docs. Include a short note about embassy processing delay. We'll open a pending review and mark the case for provisional enrollment pending final certificate.
diego: Does provisional enrollment mean coverage will be retroactive to the wedding date? I need to add dental+medical ASAP.
maya_peopleops: If approved, provisional coverage will begin on the date we can verify with acceptable docs (often the ceremony date if supported). Payroll will process any mid-month premium adjustments or retro charges. Final approval requires the conformed certificate or an apostille/translation depending on country.
nana_legal: If Peru issues a marriage record, it usually needs a legalized translation and apostille for US recognition. We can waive the apostille on provisional basis but final enrollment will require it.
diego: Thanks. Any impact on my 401(k or FSA elections? I already submitted open enroll elections.
sam_peopleops: Spouse addition affects only health/dental/vision and dependent FSA if you enroll. 401(k) beneficiary changes are separate; you can update beneficiaries anytime in Workday. If you want FSA changes mid-year, we'd need to confirm it's allowed for QLE — we'll flag the QLE request for the benefits admin to decide.
benefits-bot: Automated note: provisional enrollment requests are routed to benefits-admins@redwood.com. Expected review SLA: 3 business days. Please track status in Workday case #RB-2025-457.
diego: Uploaded affidavit + passport stamps. Marked note "marriage abroad - embassy processing delay".
maya_peopleops: Got it. We'll review and get back within 3 business days. If provisional approved, coverage effective date will be Oct 20, 2025.
payroll: Heads up: if provisional is approved, there may be retro imputed income if spouse is ineligible for pre-tax; we'll coordinate with you on net-pay adjustments.
diego: Appreciate it. Will follow up if embassy delivers earlier. Thanks everyone :party_popper:
